parsed.why: Police arrest on clothing and appearance, a 2023 moral-police investigation unit, routine extortion, trans women held in male prisons with sexual violence, and an 87% hostile public: documented state-tolerated targeting plus severe custody harm.

Criminalising statute with real 2022 and 2024 convictions, no protections, no organisations, documented stigmatisation and non-disclosure; but enforcement is episodic, no trans-specific targeting or violence is documented, and police reported no anti-LGBT violence in 2023.

Decriminalised with courts that work for trans people, but documented political hostility, LGBT-free zones, mass counter-protest violence, and a 2024 case of a trans foreign national held in a male centre with three months of HRT interrupted.

Decriminalised, pride marches proceed unimpeded, binding health non-discrimination rules, drop-in centre; but marriage recognition was legislatively revoked, hostile organised politics, and a sodomy statute retained, leaving thin rather than demonstrated recourse.

Comprehensive SOGI anti-discrimination law and legal recognition are strong positives, but enforcement is rare, support runs through civil society, official reaction to Pride violence was slow, and documented assaults and under-reported violence persist.
